documents.title: Board Meeting Outcome for Outcome Of The Board Meeting
Compliances-Certificate under Reg. 74 (5) of SEBI (DP) Regulations, 2018

analysis.summary: Amal Ltd reported consolidated sales of Rs 240 crore and standalone sales of Rs 85 crore for FY 2025-26, representing increases of 77% and 74% respectively. Growth was primarily driven by a 164% spike in the price of Sulphur, its key raw material, while volume growth contributed modestly. Profit before tax declined on both consolidated and standalone bases due to the inability to fully absorb elevated input costs. The company maintained a debt-free balance sheet with an increased cash surplus of Rs 38 crore and recommended a dividend of Rs 1.5 per share. Amal Ltd reported a strong financial performance for FY 2024-25, with consolidated sales increasing by 57% to ₹ 135 crore and PBT rising to ₹ 33 crore.

capex_expansion.claim: Amal Speciality Chemicals commissioned a new plant in 2022-23 with an equivalent capacity of 300 TPD of sulphuric products.
capex_expansion.quote: In 2022–23, ASC commissioned a new manufacturing plant with an equivalent capacity of 300 TPD of sulphuric products, strengthening the presence of our Company in its existing product portfolio.

capex_expansion.claim: The company executed two projects to improve steam generation and recovery.
capex_expansion.quote: The Company implemented two projects for better steam generation and recovery.

margins_costs.quote: The Company is implementing automation of identified operations to increase plant uptime, strengthen safety and reduce reliance on contract manpower.

capital_allocation.claim: The company repaid all of its borrowings and generated a cash surplus of ₹ 22 crore as of March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: It repaid its entire borrowing and generated cash surplus of ` 22 cr (as on March 31, 2025).

capital_allocation.claim: The company eliminated its remaining carried forward loss of ₹ 14 crore.
capital_allocation.quote: It wiped out its remaining carried forward loss of ` 14 cr which at peak was ` 56 cr.
